key_insight: Stellar Colosseum is a model-agnostic system that improves long-horizon research by managing how inference is spent across many competing solution paths. Instead of committing too early, it explores alternatives, waits until a path is ready, and then decomposes the problem more effectively.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the unreliability of language models on long, research-style problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science, where success depends on many sequential, uncertain decisions rather than a single short proof.
method: Uses a many-agent harness to allocate inference across multiple candidate research routes.
Explores alternative strategies before proof construction to avoid premature commitment.
Includes a readiness gate that determines when a route is mature enough to be broken into smaller subproblems.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical framework for scaling LLMs to harder research tasks where naive single-shot reasoning fails. It highlights a direction for building systems that are better at planning, branching, and managing uncertainty over long horizons.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing explore -> readiness gate -> decomposition -> proof construction
A branching tree of competing solution paths with one path selected for further work
An icon-based comparison of short-horizon vs long-horizon reasoning
A dashboard-style graphic showing inference allocation across multiple agents
paper_title: Stellar Colosseum: A Many-Agent Harness for Long-Horizon Research in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
paper_authors: Honghao Lin, David P. Woodruff, Yuan Deng, Jieming Mao, Song Zuo
